pages.mainText: About Jabil Bringing products to life for the world’s leading brands with engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing solutions Intense market competition is driving companies to find new ways to reduce costs, focus on their core competencies, and bring their products to market faster. At the same time, automated technologies like robotics and AI are creating transformative change for businesses in nearly every industry. Jabil goes beyond the traditional role of a manufacturing service provider. We serve as a trusted partner to the world’s leading brands across markets like AI cloud data centers, healthcare, robotics, automotive and transportation, warehouse automation, and energy. Together, we transform ideas from sketches on a napkin to the cutting-edge products that power people’s daily lives. You’ve likely interacted with at least one product today that has passed through a Jabil facility. From medical devices and digital payment solutions to data centers and semiconductor capital equipment, our expertise and capabilities extend to nearly every industry. We deliver speedy, consistent quality and service at scale through our global footprint and agile engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing solutions. GLOBAL Built for scale, engineered for impact 25+ countries 100+ sites strategically located around the world 140K+ dedicated employees worldwide 35M+ square feet of manufacturing space $29.8B revenue in FY25 400+ customers across diverse markets Our Global Locations HISTORY Our humble beginnings Jabil’s entrepreneurial founders started assembling circuit boards around a kitchen table in Michigan in 1966. Even back then, our driving force was always to find new ways to add value for our customers. VIEW OUR HISTORY OUR NAME Collaboration from the start The Jabil story begins with partnership, as founders James Golden and Bill Morean combined their first names to create the company’s. Learn how to pronounce Jabil in this video. VALUES Our common purpose: making a positive impact for employees, communities, partners, and the environment Integrity We put safety first and do what’s right by acting morally and ethically every day. Our teams across the globe take accountability and work to improve our communities and the environment. Ingenuity We think creatively, bring a positive attitude, and take an innovative approach to our work to delight our customers — moving with speed and purpose while taking calculated risks. Inspiration We respect others and embrace diversity through collaboration. Continuous improvement is at the core of our culture, so we challenge ourselves and each other while making time to build strong bonds and have fun. COMMITMENT We operate in alignment with the Jabil Code of Conduct, ensuring integrity and ethical standards in all our partnerships and operations. OUR CODE RECOGNIZED Awards and honors reflect our employees’ commitment to making a difference Newsweek America's Greatest Workplaces in Manufacturing 2025 The World’s Best Companies of 2024 by Time and Statista Fortune 2024 World’s Most Admired Companies VIEW ALL AWARDS PEOPLE Our people are our greatest strength Jabil’s dedicated employees work within a people-centered culture of trust, prioritizing safety, quality, and continuous learning. Our people are empowered to explore new pathways, take chances, and develop their talents to help them come up with the next big idea. Meet Our Leaders Job Opportunities INNOVATIVE Enabled by our global operations, Jabil’s vision is to be the world’s most technologically advanced and trusted manufacturing solutions provider. We are delivering the future of manufacturing today by building predictable manufacturing outcomes underpinned by superior asset management and operational excellence — embracing factory automation, AI, and machine learning that works alongside our people to generate continuous improvements in safety, quality, and cost. Strategic Capabilities WHY JABIL? Precise execution delivers success for our customers Jabil’s unique customer engagement model provides customers with a dedicated business unit and a single point of contact, enabling clear communication and fast decision-making. We blend Jabil’s cross-industry expertise and local knowledge with vertically integrated services across the product lifecycle to develop tailored solutions for your specific needs — anywhere in the world. We are an extension of our customers' teams, putting Jabil’s global resources and scale at your fingertips. Working with Jabil Ready to turn your possible into reality? Get In Touch Contact us.

pages.mainText: Jabil's Culture & Values A Workplace Where People and Ideas Thrive Our people are the driving force behind everything we do at Jabil. We build workplaces where innovation thrives — where every voice is heard, every idea is valued, and every employee can feel a true sense of belonging. Our relationship-based culture prioritizes safety, trust, and continuous learning. We encourage open communication and collaboration across teams and regions. At Jabil, employees are empowered to take charge of their careers, developing their skills by helping the world’s leading brands solve their toughest challenges. Here, we explore new pathways and take chances that inspire the next big breakthrough. We recognize our team members’ contributions, celebrate their ideas, and support their personal and professional growth. The culture we build together is reflected in the positive impact our teams make every day — from the way we treat each other and deliver meaningful solutions to our customers to how we give back to our local communities. Jabil’s Values We are committed to: Integrity We put safety first and do what’s right by acting morally and ethically every day. Our teams across the globe take accountability and work to improve our communities and the environment. Ingenuity We think creatively, bring a positive attitude, and take an innovative approach to our work to delight our customers — moving with speed and purpose while taking calculated risks to match the speed of technological change. Inspiration We respect others and embrace inclusivity through collaboration. Continuous improvement is at the core of our culture, so we challenge ourselves and each other while making time to build strong bonds and have fun. Doing the Right Thing We operate in alignment with the Jabil Code of Conduct, ensuring integrity and ethical standards in all our partnerships and operations. LEARN MORE Our Values in Action More than 140,000 employees bring Jabil’s core values to life through a variety of people-focused programs across our global sites. Our Commitment to Giving Back Through the Jabil Cares volunteer program, we aim to make an impact in the communities where our employees live and work, focusing on the social and environmental issues that matter most to our teams. Our employees lend their time, talents, and passion to create positive change around the globe. This commitment goes beyond business, embodying Jabil's mission to create meaningful change in the world. ABOUT JABIL CARES Employee Recognition Jabil's success starts with its people. Our Respect. Recognize. Reward. program embodies this philosophy, celebrating employees who demonstrate our values through superior performance, a commitment to helping others, and thinking big to drive Jabil forward. Making Innovation Scalable Jabil’s annual Deliver Best Practices competition showcases our employees’ commitment to innovation and collaboration. Participants submit projects that demonstrate high-impact best practices that can be replicated across our global operations and functions. Winners at the regional or functional level then present their ideas to senior leadership at Jabil's global headquarters in St. Petersburg, Florida. These finalists showcase the best of what Jabil has to offer as they compete for prizes. Empowering Every Voice Our global workforce is made up of employees from different cultures, experiences, and generations. We celebrate all these differences because they make us stronger as an organization. We foster a workplace where every employee feels welcomed, valued, and psychologically and physically safe at work. By leading with an inclusive mindset, we ensure that our organization reflects the world we operate in. Living Jabil's Culture Our culture has been the foundation of our success throughout Jabil’s 60-year history. It's experienced through purposeful actions like developing talent from within, giving our people a path to success, and making a difference in our communities. Every Jabil employee can feel safe to be their true selves and do their best work. EXPLORE CAREER OPPORTUNITIES

pages.mainText: Global Locations Jabil’s global footprint and diversified capabilities ensure speedy, consistent quality and service at scale — no matter where our customers want to make their products. Thanks to our cross-industry expertise and local knowledge, we can develop scalable, tailored solutions for our customers worldwide that meet their current needs and anticipate future requirements. This approach allows Jabil to be a true engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing partner deeply invested in the success of each customer, in any geography. 100+ manufacturing sites 25+ countries across four continents 35M+ sq. ft. of manufacturing space Our Facilities by Region Americas Jabil spans 40+ sites in the Americas, where our end-market insight and technical capabilities are pivotal in smoother supply chains worldwide. View Sites in the Americas Asia Our extensive network across Asia includes 20+ strategic locations, enabling the development of efficient global and regional supply chains. View Sites in Asia Europe and Middle East With 25+ sites throughout Europe and the Middle East, we provide key supply chain and manufacturing expertise for many of the world’s leading brands. View Sites in Europe and Middle East Our Global Footprint Enables Manufacturing at Scale Supply Chain Resilience Our global supply chain enables diversified production capabilities and reduces the risk of regional disruptions. We help secure a steady flow of materials and products, creating reliability and accessibility in meeting customer needs, everywhere. Local Expertise to Meet Local Standards Our global footprint allows us to help companies navigate complex regulations and evolving trade laws in regions around the world. As a partner to 400+ of the world’s leading brands, Jabil operates with proven expertise, necessary capabilities, and a deep understanding of the quality standards required for launching new technologies in even the most challenging markets. Innovation Through Collaboration Jabil’s worldwide network brings together a wide variety of skills, perspectives, and expertise from across the world to foster creativity and unique ideas. Our extensive involvement in fields like AI and cloud data centers, robotics, and medical devices allows us to continuously improve, adapt, and help our customers stay ahead in rapidly evolving markets. Sustainable Operations Our commitment to sustainability extends beyond our own operations, benefiting our customers and the markets they serve. Partnering with Jabil provides access to a global manufacturing network committed to reducing its carbon footprint. These efforts help our customers minimize their own environmental impact, in turn helping them meet their stakeholders’ evolving expectations. Scalability and Flexibility Having the capacity to handle large-scale production needs with geographical choice allows our customers to quickly scale up or down based on market demand and macro-level factors. Brands with a global footprint can leverage production capabilities close to the customer’s end market. This flexibility can be crucial in responding quickly to demand shifts, regulatory changes, or other challenges in the global landscape. Scale globally or regionalize your supply chain. Jabil can help. CONTACT SALES

Our Impact
pages.mainText: Jabil in the Community Local action, global impact Jabil gives back to local communities by creating opportunities for employees to get involved and drive positive change. Through our Jabil Cares community outreach and volunteer program, we empower employees around the world to take action, supporting the causes related to education, empowerment, and the environment that matter most to them. Each of our global teams brings its own passion to this mission, implementing a localized strategy that reflects the unique needs and values of their community. Throughout the year, Jabil employees worldwide volunteer their time, collaborate with local nonprofits and municipalities, and engage with community leaders to make a difference in the places where they live and work. Their hands-on involvement reflects a shared commitment to compassion, generosity, and purpose — building a better world, one community at a time. Our Impact 590K+ Volunteer Hours in 2025 639 Site-Sponsored Volunteer Events in 2025 222K+ Hours Contributed by Employees Through “Your Day, Your Cause” Volunteer PTO Day in 2025 Our Focus Areas Through volunteering, our worldwide teams aim to make a positive difference in three key areas. Education Our commitment to improving education for the next generation includes classroom grants and ensuring students have the resources they need to pursue their interests. Jabil helps equip these future leaders for success by donating books, supplies, and technology, as well as scholarships. Beyond the classroom, we invite students to tour our manufacturing sites and explore potential careers in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). We also support health education and awareness by contributing to and participating in community races, blood drives, and other charitable events. Empowerment To support individuals and communities in need, our empowerment efforts focus on providing opportunities for people with disabilities, uplifting people facing challenges, and tackling issues like food, water, and housing insecurity. Jabil Cares also organizes food drives, contributes to affordable housing projects, and offers natural disaster relief. Environment From beaches to mountain trails, our environmental initiatives enhance the natural beauty of our surroundings and make a positive impact on the planet. Jabil volunteers participate in activities like coastal habitat conservation, litter removal, and recycling programs around the world, aiming to preserve the natural environment for community enjoyment and ecological balance. Through partnerships with local organizations, our efforts also include habitat rejuvenation and reforestation to support ecosystems and combat climate change. And by teaching environmental stewardship through workshops and educational events, we strive to ensure a sustainable future for the next generation. The Power of Giving: The Jabil Cares Foundation The Jabil Cares Foundation is a nonprofit, 501(c)(3) organization of Jabil Inc., which oversees and supports Jabil’s philanthropic initiatives by partnering with nonprofit organizations (foreign and domestic) that support education, empowerment, and the environment in the communities where we operate. Living Jabil's Culture As an employee, you have the chance to make a difference in your local community and be part of something extraordinary. This commitment to making a difference in our communities is a way of life for Jabil employees. EXPLORE CAREER OPPORTUNITIES

jsonLdDescriptions: From a Detroit circuit board shop in 1966 to a $29B global manufacturer, explore Jabil's journey of innovation, strategic growth, and transformation into a world-leading electronics manufacturing services provider.
pages.mainText: Our History Jabil’s cultural DNA is rooted in our humble beginnings. Ingenuity and Early Success From the beginning, the world’s leading brands have trusted Jabil to help them make their products possible — and make them better. ’60s 1966 James Golden and William Morean enter a 50-50 partnership as Jabil, a fusion of their first names. The company starts out building circuit boards on the kitchen table of the Morean home outside Detroit, Michigan, for their first customer, Control Data corporation. 1967 Jabil receives its first production order. Previously, the company only provided printed circuit board (PCB) service orders for broken equipment. 1969 Jabil Circuit Company is incorporated. ’70s 1970 Jabil wins its second customer: General Automation, a designer and manufacturer of computers primarily for auto assembly line controllers. 1978 The company moves to a 7,200-square-foot facility in a high-tech industrial area of Troy, Michigan. 1979 General Motors awards Jabil a $15 million high-volume PCB manufacturing contract, putting Jabil on the map and allowing the company to expand its automated assembly capability. ’80s 1982 General Motors engages Jabil to help with a redesign of the Corvette's dashboard display. Jabil manufactures a component that powers the LCD display in the new car model. Jabil’s headquarters are relocated to St. Petersburg, Florida. 1985 After investing in newly developed surface-mount technology (SMT), Jabil begins highly automated volume production of circuit boards using SMT processes. 1987 Jabil establishes a prototype and design facility in San Jose, California, to research and test commercially promising technology, most notably SMT. 1989 Jabil launches its box-build operation, encasing motherboards in plastic. This marks the company's first step towards complete assembly solutions. “I’m sure my dad would be amazed to see the cultural values of accountability and empowerment intact in the global powerhouse that Jabil has become.” — BILL MOREAN, CEO (1988–2000) AND CHAIRMAN OF THE BOARD (1988–2013) ’90s 1993 Jabil opens its first international site in Scotland to provide service to customers with operations in Europe. It also makes its initial public offering on the NASDAQ stock market. 1995 Jabil expands into Asia with a factory in Penang, Malaysia, which manufactures high-end disk drive product assemblies. 1999 Jabil acquires Hong Kong-based GET Manufacturing, Inc., adding 1 million square feet of manufacturing capacity worldwide and an additional 5,000 employees. Expansion and Continuing Innovation Jabil combines its growing global reach with local expertise to deliver customized manufacturing, engineering, and supply chain solutions while building sustainable processes for the generations to come. ’00s 2001 Jabil announces plans to enter the fiber optics market and increase manufacturing capacity. A technology services division is created, complete with an optics lab. 2002 Jabil launches into the defense and aerospace market with work on guided missile electronics, night vision sensors, and aircraft radar systems. 2004 Jabil opens a 175,000-square-foot facility in Pune, India, providing a full spectrum of services for instrumentation, networking, peripherals, and telecommunications. 2007 Jabil purchases Taiwan Green Point Enterprises Company, Ltd., a state-of-the-art plastics and metals manufacturer. This adds nine factories and 30,000 new employees. Jabil is the first company of its size in the world to attain ISO 9000 quality certification. 2009 Jabil makes Newsweek's inaugural Green Rankings list, an environmental ranking of the top 500 largest publicly traded corporations. “Change and renewal has been a very important part of our story from the beginning. We’ve transitioned from a ‘board stuffer’ to a ‘solutions provider,’ from a company heavily concentrated in the communications sector to a balanced and diversified global manufacturer… We believe continuously improving what we do, with the same systems and values around the world is key to building strong, long-term relationships.” — TIMOTHY MAIN, PRESIDENT AND CEO (2000–2013), CHAIRMAN OF THE BOARD (2013–2021) ’10s 2011 The company begins construction of a new injection-molding factory in Shenzhen, China, to provide medical device manufacturers with cost-effective manufacturing services. A new photovoltaic laboratory in St. Petersburg, Florida, opens. It provides Jabil with a range of UL and IEC photovoltaic certification and testing capabilities that support the company’s manufacturing sites and its solar equipment customers. 2012 Jabil enters the electric vehicle (EV) market, leveraging decades of experience in automotive and electronics to build EV powertrains, charging components, and more for some of the world’s leading brands. 2013 Nypro, Inc. is acquired. The acquisition brings expanded capabilities in customer packaging across several industries and more than 10,000 additional employees. 2014 To meet the needs of a data-driven world, Jabil establishes its cloud data center business. This initiative is part of Jabil’s efforts to diversify revenue amongst its business units. 2017 Jabil operates in over 100 locations across more than two dozen countries. It is the world's third-largest manufacturing solutions provider. 2018 As part of a strategic collaboration with Johnson & Johnson Medical Devices (JJMD) Companies, Jabil acquires 14 JJMD sites across the Americas and Europe. The acquisition adds new capabilities for the production of orthopedic and minimally invasive surgical devices, making Jabil the largest healthcare manufacturing solutions provider in the world. Jabil scales its renewable energy business through partnerships with companies producing solar energy equipment, wind turbines, and intelligent grid management systems. “I think of going from our founders the Morean family, and their kitchen table in Michigan, to a Fortune 200 company and I think to myself, ‘That’s the kind of stuff that books and movies are made of.” — MARK MONDELLO, CEO (2013–2023) AND CHAIRMAN OF THE BOARD (2021–2026) ’20s 2022 Jabil scales its energy storage system business with the opening of its site in Salt Lake City, Utah. 2023 Within the cloud business, Jabil shifts its focus to artificial intelligence-powered cloud data centers, enabling the next generation of technologies. Jabil divests its mobility business to BYD Electronic (BYDE), with sites in Chengdu and Wuxi, China, transferring to BYDE. This divestiture is intended to better align Jabil’s technologies and capabilities with the future needs of its customers. 2024 Jabil acquires liquid cooling solutions provider Mikros Technologies to expand the company’s data center infrastructure capabilities. 2025 Jabil acquires Pharmaceutics International, Inc. (Pii) to bolster its existing portfolio of pharmaceutical solutions. 2026 Jabil marks its 60th anniversary and grows its data center power management capabilities with the acquisition of Hanley Energy Group. “As the geopolitical situation continues to evolve, our ability to adapt, combined with our designation as a U.S.-domiciled manufacturing service provider and our global footprint, is becoming increasingly important for our customers. And in my opinion, Jabil is among the best-positioned companies in the world to help customers navigate these complexities.” — MIKE DASTOOR, CEO (2024–PRESENT) Learn more about our global footprint Our Locations

pages.mainText: Senior Leadership Board of Directors Steven A. Raymund Chairman View Bio Steven A. Raymund Chairman Steven Raymund has served as a director of Jabil since January 1996. Mr. Raymund was appointed as Chairman in January 2026 and had previously been Lead Director since November 1, 2021. He retired in May 2026 from the Board of WESCO International, Inc., a multinational electronics distributor, where he also served as chair of the Audit Committee. Mr. Raymund began his career at Tech Data Corporation, a distributor of personal computer products, in 1981 as operations manager. He became COO in 1984 and was promoted to the position of CEO in 1986, serving until his retirement in 2006. Mr. Raymund served as the Chairman of the board of directors of Tech Data Corporation from 2001 until 2017. Mr. Raymund currently serves on the Board of Trustees of the Dali Museum. Mr. Raymund holds a B.S. in Economics from the University of Oregon and a Master’s Degree in International Politics from Georgetown University, School of Foreign Services. Anousheh Ansari Director View Bio Anousheh Ansari Director Anousheh Ansari has served as a director of Jabil since January 2016. She also serves on the board of directors of XOS, Inc., a manufacturer of electric commercial vehicles, since 2021. In 2018, Ms. Ansari was appointed Chief Executive Officer of XPRIZE, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that designs and implements competition models to solve world challenges. From 2006 to 2018, Ms. Ansari served as the Chief Executive Officer and continues to serve as the Chair of Prodea Systems, a privately held company she founded, which provides services and applications for in-home smart devices, networked appliances and mobile lifestyle devices. Ms. Ansari was the first female private space explorer. Ms. Ansari holds a B.S. in electronics and computer engineering from George Mason University and a master’s degree in electrical engineering from George Washington University. Mike Dastoor Chief Executive Officer and Director View Bio Mike Dastoor Chief Executive Officer and Director Michael Dastoor was named Chief Executive Officer in May 2024 and appointed as a member of the Board of Directors in September 2024. Over his 24-year tenure at Jabil, he has held multiple leadership roles across Jabil’s global markets, including serving as Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer from April 2018. Mr. Dastoor previously served as Senior Vice President, Controller from July 2010. Mr. Dastoor joined Jabil in 2000. He holds a degree in Finance and Accounting from the University of Bombay and is a Chartered Accountant from the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales. Thomas T. Edman Director View Bio Thomas T. Edman Director Thomas T. Edman recently retired from TTM Technologies Inc., where he served as Chief Executive Officer since 2014 and has been a member of its Board of Directors since 2004. Mr. Edman held multiple management roles at Applied Materials Inc., including Group Vice President and General Manager of the AKT Display Business Group and Corporate Vice President of Corporate Business Development. Before that he served as President and CEO of Applied Films Corporation and also as General Manager of the High Performance Materials Division of Marubeni Specialty Chemicals Inc. Mr. Edman is currently the Chairman of the IPC, a trade association for the electronics manufacturing industry. Mr. Edman holds a B.A. in East Asian Studies (Japan) from Yale University and an M.B.A. from The Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania. Christopher S. Holland Director View Bio Christopher S. Holland Director Christopher Holland has served as a director of Jabil since January 2018. Mr. Holland also serves on the board of directors of STERIS PLC, a healthcare and life science solutions company, since 2020. He was Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of C.R. Bard, Inc., a multinational developer, manufacturer and marketer of medical technologies and products, from 2012 to 2017. In 2015, he added responsibility for business development, corporate marketing, reimbursement, healthcare economics and strategy. From 2013 through 2015, he had responsibility for Bard Medical Division. Earlier, Mr. Holland was Senior Vice President, Finance, and Treasurer of Aramark Corporation, a global provider of food, facilities and uniform services, from 2006 through 2012; and Vice President and Treasurer from 2003 to 2006. Prior to joining Aramark, he served as Vice President and medical device sector head at J.P. Morgan and Co. from 1999 to 2003. Prior to that, Mr. Holland held various positions of increasing responsibility at J.P. Morgan. Mr. Holland holds a B.A. in economics and political science from Drew University and an MBA in finance from New York University – Leonard N. Stern School of Business. John Plant Director View Bio John Plant Director John Plant has served as a director of Jabil since January 2016. Mr. Plant is the Co-Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of Howmet Aerospace Inc., a global leader in engineered metal products. Howmet was created after the separation of Arconic Inc., where he served as Chief Executive Officer (CEO) from 2019 to 2020, and Chairman since 2017. He has served as a director of MASCO Corporation since 2012, and previously as a director of Gates Corporation from 2017 to 2019, a privately held corporation, all of which are manufacturing companies. Mr. Plant was the CEO, President and Chairman of the Board of TRW Automotive Holdings Corporation (renamed ZF TRW Automotive in 2015), a diverse automotive supplier from 2011 to 2015, and prior to that as President and CEO of TRW from 2003 to 2011. Mr. Plant has a Bachelor of Commerce in economics, accounting & law, University of Birmingham, and an Honorary Doctorate from University of Birmingham. Mr. Plant is a Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Accountants. Sujatha Chandrasekaran Director View Bio Sujatha Chandrasekaran Director Sujatha “Suja” Chandrasekaran was appointed as a director of Jabil in April 2025. Ms. Chandrasekaran has over 25 years’ experience in senior management positions at global companies, with a strong focus on technology and data, strategic transformation, digital business models, cybersecurity operations and e-commerce. Ms. Chandrasekaran has served on several boards and committees, including at American Eagle Outfitters, Brenntag and Atos. She served as Senior Executive Vice President and Chief Digital and Information Officer for CommonSpirit Health from 2019 to 2022. Prior to that, she was Global Chief Information Officer for Kimberly Clark Corporation from 2016 to 2019. She has also held senior technology roles at Walmart, The Timberland Company and PepsiCo. Ms. Chandrasekaran holds a bachelor of engineering degree from University of Madras, India; a master of business systems from Monash University, Melbourne Australia; and an Executive Development Education Certificate from London Business School. Raejeanne Skillern Director View Bio Raejeanne Skillern Director Ms. Skillern brings 30 years of experience in the enterprise and cloud computing market to the position, with an established track record of leading and growing high-profile businesses. Ms. Skillern served as Vice President and Chief Marketing Officer at Amazon Web Services from 2023 through 2025. Prior to that she served as President, Communications, Enterprise and Cloud (CEC) at Flex, Ltd., a leading technology innovation, supply chain, and manufacturing solutions company from 2019 through 2023. Prior to joining Flex in 2019, Ms. Skillern was with Intel Corporation for twenty-five years in a number of senior leadership roles, including Vice President of the Data Center Group and General Manager of the Cloud Service Provider Platform Group. Ms. Skillern holds a bachelor’s degree in mathematics and computer science from Pepperdine University, and an MBA from Marylhurst University. Tiger Tyagarajan Director View Bio Tiger Tyagarajan Director Tiger Tyagarajan was appointed as a director of Jabil in January 2024. He has served as CEO and a director of Genpact Limited since 2011. Mr. Tyagarajan is one of the industry leaders who pioneered a new global business model and transformed a division of General Electric (GE Capital International Services) into Genpact, a global professional services firm delivering digital transformation solutions for clients. Mr. Tyagarajan counsels and collaborates with C-suite executives of large global corporations, helping them implement change in their companies to improve their competitiveness. He is also on the Board of Kantar, a leading data, insights, and consulting company. Mr. Tyagarajan holds a degree in mechanical engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology, Mumbai, and a master’s degree in business administration from the Indian Institute of Management in Ahmedabad. Executive Officers Mike Dastoor Chief Executive Officer and Director View Bio Mike Dastoor Chief Executive Officer and Director Michael Dastoor was named Chief Executive Officer in May 2024 and appointed as a member of the Board of Directors in September 2024. Over his 24-year tenure at Jabil, he has held multiple leadership roles across Jabil’s global markets, including serving as Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer from April 2018. Mr. Dastoor previously served as Senior Vice President, Controller from July 2010. Mr. Dastoor joined Jabil in 2000. He holds a degree in Finance and Accounting from the University of Bombay and is a Chartered Accountant from the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales. Greg Hebard Chief Financial Officer View Bio Greg Hebard Chief Financial Officer Greg Hebard was named Chief Financial Officer in May 2024. He most recently served as Senior Vice President, Treasurer since 2021. Since joining Jabil in 2009 Mr. Hebard has held roles of increasing responsibility in finance, including Senior Vice President, CFO Green Point from 2017 to 2021 and Vice President, Financial Planning & Analysis from 2013 to 2017. He holds a master’s degree in business from DePaul University and a bachelor’s degree in finance from the University of Iowa. Andy Priestley Executive Vice President, Chief Operations Officer View Bio Andy Priestley Executive Vice President, Chief Operations Officer Andrew Priestley was named Executive Vice President, Chief Operations Officer in January 2026. He most recently served as Executive Vice President, Global Business Units since 2024. Previously, he was Senior Vice President, Global Business Units since 2014. Since joining Jabil in 1996 he has held positions of increasing responsibility across the Company. Kristine Melachrino Executive Vice President, General Counsel View Bio Kristine Melachrino Executive Vice President, General Counsel Kristine Melachrino was named Executive Vice President, General Counsel in March 2025. She most recently served as Senior Vice President, General Counsel since 2022. She joined Jabil in 2007 holding various roles in the legal department supporting the functional (Sales, Supply Chain, IT) and business teams globally. Prior to this role, Ms. Melachrino served as Vice President, Senior Deputy General Counsel for the global Commercial legal team, advising on complex legal and regulatory matters to facilitate business growth; and Assistant Corporate Secretary. Prior to joining Jabil, Ms. Melachrino was a litigation attorney responsible for all first and third-party insurance disputes under personal and commercial lines policies with Fowler White Boggs Banker’s insurance group from 2002 to 2007. She holds a Juris Doctor from Stetson University College of Law, an MBA from Stetson University, a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from University of South Florida and is a member of the Florida Bar. pages.mainText: Sustainability at Jabil DOWNLOAD REPORT To Our Employees, Customers, Investors, and Other Stakeholders At Jabil, sustainability is the integration of environmental health, social responsibility, governance, and economic growth to create thriving, healthy, diverse, and resilient business operations for our employees and the communities in which we live and work... for this generation and generations to come. We understand our responsibility to be good stewards of natural resources and positively contribute to global environmental and social challenges. We listened to our stakeholders and developed our strategy and goals in alignment with the social and environmental challenges they care about most, and the areas we believe we can make the biggest impact. We have established three pillars that form the foundation for our global sustainability efforts. Our Sustainability Pillars Our People & Communities Focusing on the health and well-being of our people and the communities in which we operate. LEARN MORE Our Operations & Resources Ensuring we operate and manage resources in our sites as efficiently as possible. LEARN MORE Our Innovative Solutions Delivering sustainable innovations throughout the product lifecycle. LEARN MORE Download our sustainability fact sheet DOWNLOAD Our Awards and Recognitions America’s Climate Leaders 2025 | USA Today EcoVadis Gold Rating | EcoVadis America’s Greenest Companies 2025 | Newsweek VIEW ALL AWARDS Contributions to the UN's Sustainable Development Goals We contribute to the achievement of the following United Nations Sustainable Development Goals: SUSTAINABILITY REPORT Download our fiscal year 2025 Sustainability Report to learn more about Jabil’s sustainability commitments, progress, and reporting. The report includes updates aligned to the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI), the Sustainable Accounting Standards Board (SASB), and the Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD). To ensure accurate reporting, Key Performance Indicators within these reports are validated internally and by external third parties. The report shows how we: Reduced enterprise-wide greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by 47% compared to our fiscal year 2019 baseline. Achieved 90%+ landfill diversion (third-party assured) at 14% of our sites. Completed over 590,000 volunteer hours in our local communities worldwide. DOWNLOAD REPORT Our Five-Year Goals Driving Meaningful Action Jabil's sustainability goals fall under three foundational pillars: Our People & Communities, Our Operations & Resources, and Our Innovative Solutions. For each goal, we set measurable KPIs and monitor their progress using data-driven dashboards. Jabil's sustainability goals are intrinsically tied with those of our customers, many of whom are the world's leading brands. In recognition of this shared objective, an integral part of our mission is to partner with and offer them our support as they strive to achieve their sustainability goals. Our People & Communities CULTURE & BELONGING 25% Of leadership positions held by women 40+ Established programs for persons with disabilities HUMAN RIGHTS ≥160 Annual global site average RBA score that equates to a silver status rating Our Operations & Resources CLIMATE ACTION 25% Reduction in operational greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions* by the end of FY25 HEALTHY ENVIRONMENT & SAFE OPERATIONS 80+ Target EHS index score RESOURCE EFFICIENCY 6% Average global reduction of our acquired or purchased water 90% or more landfill diversion achievement at 20% of applicable sites globally *Jabil’s climate action targets pertain to Jabil’s Scope 1 and Scope 2 Market-Based GHG emissions. Jabil also has longer-term climate ambitions, including a 50% reduction in operational emissions by FY30 and operational carbon neutrality by 2045, all from a FY19 baseline. searchResults.title: About Jabil
searchResults.highlight:
## Bringing products to life for the world’s leading brands with engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing solutions
...
Jabil goes beyond the traditional role of a manufacturing service provider. We serve as a trusted partner to the world’s leading brands across markets like AI cloud data centers, healthcare, robotics, automotive and transportation, warehouse automation, and energy.
...
From medical devices and digital payment solutions to data centers and semiconductor capital equipment, our expertise and capabilities extend to nearly every industry. We deliver speedy, consistent quality and service at scale through our global footprint and agile engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing solutions.
...
Enabled by our global operations, Jabil’s vision is to be the world’s most technologically advanced and trusted manufacturing solutions provider. We are delivering the future of manufacturing today by building predictable manufacturing outcomes underpinned by superior asset management and operational excellence — embracing factory automation, AI, and machine learning that works alongside our people to generate continuous improvements in safety, quality, and cost.
...
Jabil’s unique customer engagement model provides customers with a dedicated business unit and a single point of contact, enabling clear communication and fast decision-making. We blend Jabil’s cross-industry expertise and local knowledge with vertically integrated services across the product lifecycle to develop tailored solutions for your specific needs — anywhere in the world. We are an extension of our customers' teams, putting Jabil’s global resources and scale at your fingertips.

Jabil | Engineering, Supply Chain & Manufacturing Solutions | Jabil

Engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing that enables the world’s leading product brands.
...
Our team helps the world’s leading brands design, build, and scale products across global markets. Leveraging more than 60 years of experience across nearly every industry, we solve their toughest challenges by leading with engineering, forging resilient supply chains, and delivering comprehensive manufacturing solutions.
...
## WHAT WE DO
...
Tailored solutions across the product lifecycle accelerate your time-to-market
...
Design & Engineering
...
Our 9,000+ engineers partner with customers from prototype to final production, engaging early in product development to ensure designs are functional, manufacturable, and market-ready.
...
Supply Chain Management
...
Backed by our $30 billion annual purchasing spend and global network of 38,000-plus suppliers, we help accelerate product development by mitigating risk in our customers’ supply chain by leveraging proven expertise, processes, and technology.
...
Jabil’s manufacturing models are personalized to each customer’s specific production needs, all led by our focus on consistently delivering the highest quality products.
...
Post-Production
...
We help our customers maximize the valuable life of their products and electronic components through return, refurbishment, and repair services, reducing their environmental impact and improving compliance with shifting regulations.

searchResults.title: Jabil's Solutions: Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Manufacturing | Jabil
searchResults.highlight:
Jabil's Solutions: Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Manufacturing | Jabil
...
From design and manufacturing to delivery and beyond, Jabil has you covered
...
Our vertically integrated model covers the entire product lifecycle — from innovation and design to sourcing, manufacturing, delivery, and service. With deep engineering expertise, advanced technologies, and a global supply chain, we streamline every step of the product lifecycle to increase efficiency and quality.
...
Jabil acts as a strategic partner to help you accelerate time-to-market, reduce risk, and stay competitive in a fast-moving global market. Whether you're launching a new product or scaling operations, we ensure every step of the lifecycle is aligned with your business goals.
...
With over 50 years of experience as a trusted manufacturing partner to hundreds of the world’s leading brands, Jabil understands that the greatest opportunity to optimize a product is in its earliest stages. Backed by a global team of 140,000 employees across 100 sites in more than 25 countries, we bring deep cross-industry expertise to help you identify the smartest path forward — accelerating time-to-market, improving yields, reducing costs, and turning complex ideas into reality.
...
Maximizing your product’s potential starts with early collaboration. At Jabil, we engage with your team from the concept phase, giving you access to thousands of experienced engineers across multiple domains, each focused on optimizing your design for performance, manufacturability, and scalability.
...
The development phase will bring your product from concept to reality. At Jabil, we work closely with your team to build a strategic roadmap that guides your design through prototyping and into full-scale production.
...
Our engineering, design, and other cross-functional teams collaborate with you to fine-tune your product, optimize manufacturing processes, and manage procurement. We focus on improving manufacturability, boosting performance, and strengthening supply chain resilience.
...
We align material planning with real-world demand by combining advanced forecasting tools, real-time data, and deep supply chain expertise. Through predictive analytics and close collaboration with customers and suppliers, we make sourcing decisions that are proactive, cost-effective, and tightly integrated with downstream operations — reducing lead times, minimizing waste, and accelerating time-to-market.
...
With visibility into more than 700,000 parts and a network of 38,000 global suppliers, we offer deep insights into commodity trends, sourcing strategies, and potential supply chain shortages. Our close collaboration with this broad, agile supplier base gives us a clear understanding of technology dependencies and geographic vulnerabilities — enabling us to proactively mitigate disruptions through multi-location manufacturing and dual sourcing. This integrated approach ensures continuity, flexibility, and resilience, even in the most constrained or volatile markets.
...
We apply advanced manufacturing technologies to make production faster, more efficient, and high in quality. Together with your team, we determine the right mix of capabilities — ranging from robotics, miniaturization, digitization, and precision automation to machine learning and artificial intelligence — to meet your product’s unique requirements.
...
Jabil ensures your products reach the right place at the right time. Our customer-specific advanced analytics dashboards offer real-time visibility into shipment status, carrier performance, and delivery metrics, enabling proactive decision-making and continuous improvement.
...
Through predictive logistics, advanced freight management, and close coordination with global carriers, we take full ownership of your supply chain management. This allows you to stay focused on your core business while we deliver a seamless, cost-efficient logistics experience that enhances customer satisfaction and reinforces supply chain confidence.
...
Jabil’s after-market service solutions go beyond warranty coverage. They’re designed to extend product life, reduce waste, and support a more sustainable future. During the warranty period, we manage repairs and replacements at no additional cost, ensuring minimal disruption for your customers. Our intuitive customer service portal enables real-time tracking, collaboration, and communication, making support seamless and transparent.
...
But after-market service doesn’t stop at repair. It plays a critical part in the circular economy. We help you plan for longevity from the start, using modular design, responsible material sourcing, and strategic supplier partnerships to make products easier to maintain, upgrade, and recycle. By integrating service with circularity, we help you reduce environmental impact while delivering long-term value to your customers.

Our consultative approach, backed by deep engineering and hardware expertise, ensures every solution is built for long-term performance and seamless integration. Automation is embedded into our factory systems through standardized processes and rigorous design guidelines, enabling consistent execution and faster time to market across our global network.

Jabil is one of the world’s leading electronics manufacturing services (EMS) providers, trusted by customers to deliver complex, high-performance electronic solutions from initial prototype to full-scale production. With a focus on precision, scalability, and speed, Jabil consistently meets exacting specifications while maintaining the highest standards of quality.
...
Jabil’s industry-leading supply chain and product lifecycle management capabilities enable efficient, reliable large form factor assembly solutions. With more than a dozen global facilities tailored for large form factor assembly, Jabil delivers the expertise and infrastructure needed to support your most ambitious builds.
...
Jabil’s advanced metals capabilities deliver the ideal balance of performance, quality, sustainability, and cost-efficiency to meet diverse product requirements. From precision components for automotive and aerospace applications to surgical instruments and consumer electronics, Jabil produces high-quality metal solutions that support innovation across industries.
...
Jabil’s optics capabilities are designed to meet today’s most complex challenges with end-to-end support across design, engineering, and production. Leveraging decades of experience and a global footprint, we deliver tailored manufacturing solutions that accelerate development, ensure scalability, and maintain quality from concept to mass production. Our optics engineers work within Jabil’s integrated ecosystem, gaining direct access to advanced tools, cross-functional expertise, and cutting-edge processes, enabling agile innovation and consistent execution. Trusted by leading brands across industries, we bring high-performance optical solutions to life for applications such as LiDAR, 3D sensing, imaging, and projection.
...
Jabil’s vertically integrated plastics manufacturing capabilities accelerate product development, ensure consistent quality, and reduce total cost from prototype to production. As a one-stop partner, we offer expertise in injection molding, liquid silicone rubber molding, plastics assembly, inspection and test development, and additive manufacturing to deliver reliable solutions tailored to your needs.
...
Jabil brings over a decade of experience in photonics, delivering customized solutions from high-speed transceivers to co-packaged optics. Our comprehensive capabilities span optical manufacturing services, advanced photonics packaging, design expertise, and flexible platform engagement models. Whether you need turnkey components or white-label options, Jabil’s integrated approach ensures precision, scalability, and speed-to-market for cutting-edge photonics applications.
